notes.text: Nathan MacKinnon is out (lower-body injury) and has missed the last 3 games. He is one of their most valuable skaters. Brock Nelson has taken his spot beside Artturi Lehkonen and Martin Nečas.

Cale Makar is on injured reserve and has missed the last 3 games. He is a top-pair defenseman. Sam Malinski has taken his spot beside Devon Toews. That pair has had 65% of the chances at 5-on-5 in 39:52 together, about what it had with Makar (61%).
Mike Reilly was added to the roster on Nov 16.
Zachary L'Heureux is no longer killing penalties: 3% of the team’s shorthanded time in 3 games, down from 36% with his old team last season.
Quinn Hughes is day to day (upper-body injury), reported after he played in their last game. He is one of their most valuable skaters.
Yakov Trenin is away for personal reasons and missed their last game. Nico Sturm has taken his spot beside Danila Yurov and Maxim Shabanov.
Olli Määttä is out (upper body injury) and has missed the last 2 games. Brock Faber has taken his spot beside Jonas Brodin.
Marcus Foligno is no longer killing penalties: 4% of the team’s shorthanded time in 10 games, down from 34% last season.

stakes: The Avalanche go in third in the Central with 29 points, 9 points behind the Wild, first in the NHL.

MIN.head: Leaning the Wild’s way
MIN.body: Minnesota may be without Hughes, while Colorado has been out-chancing opponents lately. Then again, Colorado will be without MacKinnon, and Minnesota has home-ice advantage. Still, it’s close: the Avalanche can make it interesting if they keep the shots coming.

COL.head: Close, but the Wild have the slight edge
COL.body: Colorado will be without MacKinnon, while Minnesota has home-ice advantage. Then again, Minnesota may be without Hughes, and Colorado has been out-chancing opponents lately. The Avalanche can tip it if they keep the shots coming.

story.head: Kaprizov’s favorite opponent
paras: The Wild have won five straight, and they’re rolling. The Avalanche (13-7-3) beat Anaheim 4-0 on Nov 19. Two of the league’s best teams meet. Going in, the Avs are third in the Central (tied for tenth in the NHL) and the Wild are first in the NHL.

The Avalanche’s record (.630) is about what their chances are worth. The Wild’s record (.792) is running ahead of what their chances are worth (.636), largely thanks to their goaltending. If the Wild’s record were closer to their chances, like the Avalanche’s, these teams would be much closer in the standings, so don’t be surprised if this one is closer than the records suggest.
In their five-game winning streak, the Wild have outscored teams 24-9, including 16-7 at 5-on-5.

The Avalanche do a lot of their shooting from distance (lowest). They also get their defensemen shooting (2nd), so their defensemen shoot a lot, and the Wild’s not so much. Colorado has scored 3.91 goals a game, the second most in the league. As for the Wild, they draw more penalties than they take (2nd) and have had some of the league’s best goaltending (2nd), but get pinned in their own end on long shifts (32nd). Minnesota has allowed 2.17 goals a game, the fewest in the league. Both teams like to play fast, especially the Avalanche (1st), so expect an open game.

Martin Nečas (10 G / 16 A / 26 P in 23 GP) leads the Avalanche in scoring, and Artturi Lehkonen (15 G / 6 A / 21 P in 23 GP) has a team-high 15 goals, fifth in the NHL. Kirill Kaprizov (18 G / 25 A / 43 P in 24 GP) leads the Wild in scoring and is third in the NHL, with twelve points in his last five games and a point in eight straight games against Colorado.
Mackenzie Blackwood (11-4-1 / .904 SV% in 16 GS) is in line to start for Colorado. Jesper Wallstedt (16-2-3 / .925 SV% in 21 GS) has been outstanding for Minnesota and will likely start.
